cover.title:
Primes and
**GCD**
cover.lead: Count primes below n by crossing out multiples; get a GCD by taking remainders until one is zero.
cover.use_it_when: A problem asks how many primes are below n, or for the GCD of two numbers.
cover.why_it_matters: Both come back in fraction, divisor and counting problems.
cover.promise: You'll write the sieve in {lines} lines.

slides.title: A number chart
slides.scene: On a chart of numbers, circle 2 and cross out its multiples. Circle the next number left standing, cross out its multiples, and so on.

blocks.text: Whatever no smaller number divides is [[prime]].

slides.title: Cross out multiples
slides.lead: For each prime p, cross out p × p, p × p + p, and so on.

quickcheck.question: How many primes are there below 30?

slides.label: WHY START AT p × p
slides.teaser: The answer, then why p × p
slides.title: Start at p × p

blocks.text: Every multiple of p below p × p has a smaller factor, so a smaller prime already crossed it out. That's also why the loop stops once p × p ≥ n.
gcd(18, 12): 18 mod 12 = 6, then 12 mod 6 = 0, so the GCD is {{gcd(18, 12)}}.

slides.title: Count primes

lines: isPrime = array of n values, all true
set isPrime[0] and isPrime[1] to false
return number of true values in isPrime

slides.explain: Line 9 starts at p × p; line 5 keeps 0 and 1 out.

slides.title: Mark 0 and 1
slides.lead: 0 and 1 start as true. Skip line 5 and they get counted.

cost.note: Testing each number on its own costs O(n √n).

blog.summary: Count primes below n by crossing out multiples; get a GCD by taking remainders until one is zero.
blog.tested_inputs: hand-picked cases (n of 0, 1, 2, 3, 30 and 5,000,000; GCDs with a zero, coprime pairs, equal numbers, large numbers) and random n up to 2,000 and random pairs up to 1,000,000
blog.tested_against: trial division for primes and the largest common divisor found by trying every divisor
blog.tested_extra: The crossed-out numbers, both answers and the trap result come from running the code.

caption.first: The Sieve of Eratosthenes for LeetCode 204 Count Primes, plus Euclid's GCD by remainders.
lines: For each prime p, cross out p × p, p × p + p, … and stop when p × p ≥ n.
The trap: forget to mark 0 and 1 and countPrimes(10) gives 6, not 4.
